key_insight: EM-DETR combines heterogeneous medical imaging datasets with example-based grounding to improve multi-domain lesion detection.
clinical_relevance: The approach could support more adaptable computer-aided detection across chest X-rays and mammography, but clinical benefit is not established.
method: Combine datasets annotated for anatomical structures and abnormalities.
Use student–teacher training to reconcile differing label spaces and mitigate catastrophic forgetting.
Extend example-based EM-DETR to jointly learn detection across domains.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports image-level AUC gains exceeding 1 percentage point over prior state of the art for four chest X-ray findings, plus mAP50 gains of 2–3 percentage points over single-dataset EM-DETR in chest X-rays and mammography.
watch_item: The abstract does not specify dataset sizes or external validation, leaving generalizability to new clinical settings uncertain.
paper_title: Toward Foundation Detection Models via Example-Based Grounding in EM-DETR
